proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the unrestricted regular-grid MSE and honest-length orders, strengthened them to the published fixed-parameter class by a scaled-class sandwich, and established a four-unit normalized-class nonlinear comparison. Kallenberg kernel randomization was attested before the authoritative rerun, which passed math but capped novelty at subfield (7.1 below 7.4); independent D and main validity reviews found no bounded field lift. Ballast hygiene and conservative interval informativeness remain disclosed; formalization was not entered and no Lean proof, axiom audit or accepted-tier certification is claimed.
tldr: For every fixed \(c>0\), \(\overline Y>0\), and \(\gamma>0\), one randomized intervention on the regular-grid published power-decay class has unrestricted minimax mean-square order \(R_N^{\mathrm{FN}}\asymp N^{-\gamma/(\gamma+1)}\) and uniformly honest expected-length order \(H_N^{\mathrm{FN}}\asymp N^{-\gamma/(2\gamma+2)}\). The fixed-scale block-intercept mixture proves the lower bound against every table-independent assignment law and every measurable randomized analysis. The credited growing-cluster exposure construction attains these orders with explicit finite-sample certificates. The normalized class supplies the internal constants; the existing class sandwich, exact decision-scale equivariance, and risk-transfer lemma give the published-class theorem directly in its declared criteria and procedures. Nonlinear analysis cannot improve the worst-case polynomial exponent. A separate four-unit theorem proves strict improvement over optimized affine risk on the full normalized class for \(\gamma\ge7\); that strict comparison is not asserted for the larger published class.
gap: Theorem 1 and Equation (3) of \cite{FaridaniNiehaus2026} give an all-design frontier for assignment-weighted linear analyses. The unrestricted neighborhood theory of \cite{KandirosHarshawSavje2026} does not supply a converse inside the coupled all-radius spatial class.
fill: The theorem target is a legal small-gate embedding with fixed-scale nuisance uncertainty, complete-experiment distance control under every allocation, and matching exposure-based risk and interval certificates. The contribution is the unrestricted converse and the honest-length characterization; the clustering strategy and the polynomial exponent are credited prior work.
